description: Fig. 1 is a two-panel micrograph group (metallographic/back-scattered-type images of etched Fe-Mn-Al-C lightweight steel) comparing discontinuous precipitation after 600 °C tempering. Both panels carry a horizontal 100 µm scale bar in the bottom-right corner and show a strongly banded, rolling-direction-aligned microstructure; neither bears a printed panel letter, so the (a)/(b) assignment follows the caption. Panel (a) is the 9Al-10Mn-0.4C alloy: a light grey matrix (austenite) traversed by dark, elongated band-shaped regions, with parts of the grains showing a fine lamellar (pearlite-like) constituent, consistent with only partial discontinuous precipitation. Panel (b) is the 9Al-10Mn-1C alloy: a darker, heavily transformed matrix crossed by numerous bright white elongated bands and stringers; the transformation is far more extensive than in (a). Together the panels demonstrate that raising carbon from 0.4 to 1C markedly increases the extent of austenite decomposition into γ + κ lamellar structure during 600 °C tempering, with only limited band-shaped austenite regions surviving in (b). No numeric data, phase labels or indices are printed on either panel; all phase assignments come from the caption and citing text.

subfigures.description: Micrograph of 600 °C tempered 9Al-10Mn-0.4C. Light grey matrix with dark elongated band-shaped regions aligned horizontally; some grains contain a fine lamellar constituent, indicating partial discontinuous precipitation. 100 µm scale bar bottom-right.
Micrograph of 600 °C tempered 9Al-10Mn-1C. Darker, more extensively transformed matrix crossed by many bright white elongated bands/stringers aligned horizontally. 100 µm scale bar bottom-right.

observations.observation: Both panels are micrographs with a horizontal 100 µm scale bar in the bottom-right corner.
Panel (a) shows a light grey matrix containing dark, elongated band-shaped regions aligned along a common (horizontal) direction, with local fine lamellar structure inside some regions.
Panel (b) shows a darker matrix crossed by numerous bright white elongated bands/stringers in the same horizontal direction, i.e. a more heavily transformed appearance than (a).
Neither panel contains printed panel letters, phase labels, axes, indices or numeric data values.
The caption states the figure shows discontinuous precipitation in 600 °C tempered alloys 9Al-10Mn-0.4C (a) and 9Al-10Mn-1C (b).
The citing text states that at 9Al-10Mn-0.4C the grains underwent only partial discontinuous precipitation (Fig. 1(a)).
The citing text states that at 9Al-10Mn-1C almost all the austenite volume was transformed into γ + κ lamellar structure (Fig. 1(b)).
The citing text states that only a few γ band-shaped regions survived the transformation in the 9Al-10Mn-1C microstructure shown in Fig. 1(b).
The citing text states that austenite evolved through discontinuous precipitation into γ + κ lamellar structures, and that some δ-phase might also be present in the transformed lamellar structure.
The citing text links the microstructures to a hardness increase in the grades treated at 600 °C (Table 2, Fig. 1).

The citing text compares these panels with 9% Al alloys (Fig. 1(a)) where austenite grains only partially transformed versus 12% Al where the whole volume reacted, attributing the difference to higher Al driving force.
